Internal helper: the stop for results that cannot share a table

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_table_split_stop.Rd

Ruling R56 (Session 406): one jtable() call makes one table, so the user decides what goes together, and a list that cannot make one table stops. The stop names what keeps the results apart, then gives the lines that make each table – the results that can share one grouped, in the order of each table's first result – and the line that writes them to one file. Before it says so, each line's table is built (and discarded), so a result that cannot make a table at all stops in its own words, and no offered line stops again (ruling R23). style = goes on every line, a table type's setting on the lines of the tables that take it, and the file, overwrite =, open =, landscape = and print = on the line that writes; headings =, markers =, title = and note = name one table, and a sentence says to put them on its line.

Usage

.jst_table_split_stop(
  results,
  groups,
  x_sub,
  env,
  st,
  over_q,
  over_vals,
  given,
  mc
)

Arguments

results

A list of results.

groups

The tables' results (.jst_table_share_groups()).

x_sub

The call's first argument as typed.

env

The caller's environment.

st

The call's style.

over_q, over_vals

The call's style settings: as typed (quosures) and evaluated.

given

Logical, named headings, markers, title, note: which of them the call gave.

mc

The matched call.
